claims.text: A newly developed computational potential can accurately capture the diverse atomic configurations of high-entropy alloys.
The new potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The new potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at high melting temperatures.
The proposed potential is designed to represent the diverse atomic configurations of high-entropy alloys.
The potential is applicable to unspecified multielement high-entropy-alloy compositions, particularly near their melting temperatures.
Atomic interactions modeled by the new potential constitute the structural mediator.
More accurate representation of liquid-state atomic configurations will enhance overlap between the reference and target phase spaces.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will improve the accuracy of predicted thermodynamic properties.
The proposed applicability excludes non-high-entropy-alloy systems and lower-temperature regimes.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction will depend on the characteristics of the potential.
